name: 00-clean-30
why: the control: clean 30 fps, soft 25 µs edges

name: 01-clean-23976
why: clean 23.976: must be told apart from 24 by measuring, one part in 1000

name: 02-drop-minute
why: 29.97 drop across 00:00:59;20 → 00:01:00;02: the skipped numbers must not appear

name: 03-drop-tenth
why: 29.97 drop across the tenth minute: 00:09:59;29 → 00:10:00;00, nothing skipped

name: 04-inverted
why: polarity flipped by a miswired cable: the level carries nothing

name: 05-quiet
why: -46 dBFS, barely there, no noise: louder is not better

name: 06-hot-clipped
why: +24 dB into a hard clip: a square wave hardly minds

name: 07-noise-20dB
why: white noise 20 dB down

name: 08-noise-6dB
why: white noise only 6 dB down: a bad line

name: 09-hum
why: mains hum at 60 Hz, as loud as the code itself

name: 10-dc-offset
why: a DC offset of 40% of the level: every crossing moves

name: 11-highpass-300
why: a 300 Hz high-pass (a phone line, a vocal channel's low cut): the flat tops sag

name: 12-lowpass-3k
why: a 3 kHz low-pass at 30 fps (a cheap codec, a long cable): the edges smear into each other

name: 13-eq-peak
why: someone thought it was music: +12 dB at 2 kHz, Q 2

name: 14-compressor
why: a broadcast compressor, 10:1 with make-up gain

name: 15-mp3-128
why: round trip through MP3 at 128 kbps, 44.1 kHz

name: 16-mp3-32
why: round trip through MP3 at 32 kbps: the codec gives up on high frequencies

name: 17-44k1
why: 30 fps at 44.1 kHz: a bit is 18.375 samples, never a whole number

name: 18-8k
why: 30 fps at 8 kHz: a half bit is 1.67 samples

name: 19-wrong-clock
why: rendered at 48 kHz, played by a card running at 44.1: 8.1% slow, every pitch drops
note: reads at the wrong speed by design: its rate should NOT name 30

name: 20-varispeed-half
why: tape at half speed

name: 21-varispeed-x4
why: shuttle at 4×

name: 22-tape-stop
why: the tape slows from 1× to 0.2× and keeps reading

name: 23-reverse
why: played backward: GoButton's reader is forward-only, so this is the room's open door

name: 24-dropout
why: 200 ms of silence in the middle: the reader must lose lock and find it again
note: 6 frames are silent and 1 is cut on each side of the gap; with the start and the end, 10 no reader can read. A careful reader spends one more confirming at the start and one after the gap: 12

name: 25-rate-change
why: 25 fps, then a cut to 29.97 drop: one reader, no setting, must follow
